html:
This is the hands-on workbook behind every "Show answer" exercise in the CPQ & Revenue Cloud Academy. By the end you will have completed 31 exercises, 10 mini projects, and 1 capstone — a portfolio you can show any hiring manager.

Every exercise reuses the academy's objects and services only: Discount_Schedule__c, Revenue_Schedule__c, Renewal_Opportunity__c, Approval_Log__c, Training_Question__c, the custom fields on Account, Opportunity, Quote, QuoteLineItem, Contract and Order, the Revenue_Sync__e platform event, and the ten services QuoteCalculatorService, BundleConfigurationService, PriceRuleEngineService, ApprovalRoutingService, ContractGenerationService, RenewalQuoteService, OrderFulfillmentService, BillingScheduleService, RevenueRecognitionService, QuoteTriggerHandlerService. API version 68.0.

How to use this workbook

  • Work through the phases in order; exercise ids (e.g. 4.2) match the in-app "Show answer" panel exactly, so try each one from memory first, then compare.
  • Paste the Verify line into Developer Console / the SOQL Query Editor to prove your work. Code exercises compile against the service classes in force-app/main/default/classes.
  • Any exercise that writes data through triggers must respect QuoteTriggerHandlerService.shouldRun / clear recursion guards — loop errors mean a guard is missing.
  • Difficulty: ★ = quick task, up to ★★★★★ = capstone-grade. Keep a progress log; the capstone (CAP) wires your best artifacts together.

Phase 1 — CPQ & Revenue Cloud Fundamentals

1.1 Map the Quote-to-Cash Lifecycle ★

Goal: Draw the end-to-end lifecycle with the primary record at each stage.

  1. Draw the chain: Lead -> Opportunity -> Quote -> Approval -> Contract -> Order -> Fulfillment -> Billing -> Revenue Recognition -> Renewal.
  2. Label each node with its record: Quote/QuoteLineItem, Contract, Order, Revenue_Schedule__c, Renewal_Opportunity__c.
  3. Mark which stages are legacy CPQ (SBQQ__ package) vs RLM (core objects) and add two validation gates: config validity before pricing, approval status before contract.

Verify: Every stage is present, each has a record, and both engines are labeled correctly.

1.2 Choose CPQ vs RLM for a Scenario ★★

Goal: Pick the engine for three scenarios and justify in two sentences each.

  1. Enterprise hardware+services bundle with heavy approvals -> legacy CPQ (SBQQ__Quote, configurator, approval matrices).
  2. Fast-growing SaaS needing unified catalog + native billing on core objects -> RLM (ProductCatalog, ProductSellingModel).
  3. Existing CPQ wanting co-termination + recognition dashboards -> hybrid (CPQ quotes, Revenue Cloud handles billing/recognition).

Verify: A->legacy, B->RLM, C->hybrid, each naming the objects that justify it.

Phase 2 — Product Catalog & Configuration

2.1 Model a Product Catalog ★★

Goal: Build 5 SaaS products across 2 families and price them.

  1. Create 5 Product2 records (Starter, Growth, Scale, Enterprise, Add-on Pack) with Family Subscription or Add-on.
  2. Add each to the standard price book as a PricebookEntry with a list price.
  3. Ready List_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c, ARR__c on QuoteLineItem.

Verify: SELECT COUNT() FROM Product2 WHERE Family = 'Subscription' is correct and each product has one standard PricebookEntry.

2.2 Configure Product Options & Features ★★

Goal: Model selectable options and a single-select group.

  1. On Scale define two feature groups: Storage and Support, each with priced options and a default.
  2. On QuoteLineItem store the choice as Bundle_Option__c = <Group>: <Option>; parents get Is_Bundle_Parent__c = true.
  3. Make Storage single-select.

Verify: Selecting two different Storage options on one quote produces exactly one conflict — matching BundleConfigurationService.hasConflictingOptions returning true.

Phase 3 — CPQ Data Model & Object Relationships

3.1 Build the CPQ Data Model (ERD) ★★

Goal: Draw the academy's ERD with cardinality.

  1. Draw Account 1-N Opportunity 1-N Quote 1-N QuoteLineItem.
  2. Add Quote 1-1 Contract, Contract 1-N Renewal_Opportunity__c, Order 1-N Revenue_Schedule__c.
  3. Place the ARR fields (Account.Current_ARR__c, Opportunity.ARR__c, Quote.Total_ARR__c, Contract.ARR__c, Order.Total_ARR__c) and the Approval_Log__c.Quote__c lookup.

Verify: Every relationship shows source, target, and cardinality; all fields from the academy data model are placed.

3.2 Query the CPQ Data Model with SOQL ★★

Goal: Traverse the model with SOQL in the Query Editor.

soql
SELECT Id, QuoteId, Product2.Name, Quantity, UnitPrice, List_Unit_Price__c,
       Net_Unit_Price__c, Discount_Percent__c, ARR__c
FROM QuoteLineItem
WHERE Quote.Opportunity.StageName = 'Closed Won'
soql
SELECT ARR__c, Auto_Renew__c, Uplift_Percent__c,
       (SELECT ARR__c, Renewal_Date__c, Status__c FROM Renewal_Opportunities__r)
FROM Contract ORDER BY ARR__c DESC

Verify: Query 1 lists won-deal lines with discount + ARR; query 2 sorts contracts by ARR with renewals; add GROUP BY Recognition_Method__c over Revenue_Schedule__c as the third.

Phase 4 — Bundles, Product Rules & Configuration

4.1 Design a Bundle with Product Rules ★★★

Goal: Design one configurable server bundle.

  1. One parent QuoteLineItem with Is_Bundle_Parent__c = true, price 0.
  2. Options using "Group: Option": Storage: 100/250 GB, Compute: 8/16 vCPU, Support: Basic/Silver; label price 0 on the parent (bundle price = sum of options).
  3. Enforce single-select per group; any valid Storage + Compute + Support combination is allowed.

Verify: validateBundleConfiguration(lines) is empty and hasConflictingOptions is false with one option per group, true when two Storage options are selected.

4.2 Validate a Bundle Configuration in Apex ★★★

Goal: Validate and price a bundle in memory, no DML.

apex
List<QuoteLineItem> lines = new List<QuoteLineItem>();
lines.add(new QuoteLineItem(Is_Bundle_Parent__c = true, Quantity = 1));
lines.add(new QuoteLineItem(Bundle_Option__c = 'Storage: 250 GB', Quantity = 1, Net_Unit_Price__c = 350));
lines.add(new QuoteLineItem(Bundle_Option__c = 'Support: Silver', Quantity = 1, Net_Unit_Price__c = 150));
System.debug(BundleConfigurationService.validateBundleConfiguration(lines));
System.debug(BundleConfigurationService.rollupBundlePrice(lines));

Verify: Issues: [] and Rollup: 500.00; adding a second Storage line raises one conflict.

Phase 5 — Pricing, Price Rules & Discounting

5.1 Create a Tiered Discount Schedule ★★

Goal: Insert a volume schedule on Discount_Schedule__c.

  1. Three Volume rows, Active__c = true: 0-9999 = 0%, 10000-49999 = 5%, 50000+ = 10%; set Product_Family__c = 'Subscription'.
  2. Add a blank-family fallback so non-Subscription products never match a wrong tier.

Verify: PriceRuleEngineService.resolveDiscountPercent('Subscription', 25000) = 5.00, at 75000 = 10.00, at 1000 = 0.00.

5.2 Write a Volume-Based Price Rule ★★★

Goal: Apply tiers to a batch of lines like a trigger would.

apex
List<QuoteLineItem> lines = [SELECT Id, PricebookEntryId, List_Unit_Price__c FROM QuoteLineItem LIMIT 50];
Map<Id, Decimal> disc = PriceRuleEngineService.applyPriceRules(lines);
for (QuoteLineItem li : lines) {
    Decimal d = disc.get(li.Id) == null ? 0 : disc.get(li.Id);
    li.Discount_Percent__c = d;
    li.Net_Unit_Price__c = li.List_Unit_Price__c * (1 - d / 100);
}

Verify: A $1000 line hits the 5% tier (Net_Unit_Price__c = 950.00), a $60k line the 10% tier; the map is keyed by line Id.

Phase 6 — Quote Templates & Document Generation

6.1 Build a Quote Template ★★

Goal: A reusable template that renders a real quote.

  1. Header/footer surface account name and quote number.
  2. Line table: Product, Qty, List, Discount %, Net, ARR; footer totals incl. Total_ARR__c and term from Contract_Term_Months__c.

Verify: Generated document matches the quote's line items and total dollar-for-dollar.

6.2 Design a Multi-Language Quote Layout ★★★

Goal: One quote, two languages.

  1. List hard-coded labels from 6.1, create a second template with translated headers (naming Quote_ES), bind the same fields.

Verify: Both templates render identical dollar amounts and switching user locale serves the translated document.

Phase 7 — Approval Processes & Advanced Approvals

7.1 Route Discount Approvals by Threshold ★★★

Goal: Route by discount using ApprovalRoutingService.

apex
Decimal dp = 32.50;
System.debug(ApprovalRoutingService.requiresApproval(dp));     // true
System.debug(ApprovalRoutingService.determineApprover(dp));    // Id or null
Approval_Log__c log = ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(
    [SELECT Id FROM Quote LIMIT 1].Id, 'Pending', dp, 'Above threshold');
System.debug(log.Approval_Type__c);                            // 'Discount (Executive)'

Verify: requiresApproval(25.00) is false, (25.01) is true, and the log row shows Approval_Type__c = 'Discount (Executive)'.

7.2 Implement an Approval Chain in Apex ★★★

Goal: Two-step chain (manager then executive).

  1. Log a manager hop (Approval_Type__c = 'Discount (Manager)', Decision__c = 'Approved').
  2. Only if approved and requiresApproval holds, log the executive hop; each hop gets its own Decision_Date__c.
apex
Id qid = [SELECT Id FROM Quote LIMIT 1].Id;
ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(qid, 'Approved', 30.00, 'Manager ok');
if (ApprovalRoutingService.requiresApproval(30.00)) {
    ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(qid, 'Approved', 30.00, 'Executive ok');
}

Verify: SELECT Approval_Type__c, Decision__c, Decision_Date__c FROM Approval_Log__c WHERE Quote__c = :qid ORDER BY Decision_Date__c returns manager then executive; a 24% quote stops at the manager.

Phase 8 — Contracts, Amendments & Renewals

8.1 Generate a Contract from a Quote ★★

Goal: Materialize a won quote into a Draft contract.

apex
Quote q = new Quote(Name = 'Q-2000',
    AccountId = [SELECT Id FROM Account LIMIT 1].Id,
    Total_ARR__c = 24000, Contract_Term_Months__c = 12, Is_Renewal__c = false);
insert q;
Contract c = ContractGenerationService.generateContract(q);

Verify: Status = 'Draft', ContractTerm = 12, ARR__c = 24000.00, Auto_Renew__c = false (true when Is_Renewal__c = true).

8.2 Automate Renewal Uplift ★★★

Goal: Predict renewal value with uplift.

apex
System.debug(RenewalQuoteService.calculateUpliftedARR(100000, 7.5)); // 107500.00
Contract c = [SELECT Id, ARR__c, Uplift_Percent__c, StartDate, EndDate, ContractTerm
              FROM Contract WHERE Status = 'Signed' LIMIT 1];
Renewal_Opportunity__c opp = RenewalQuoteService.buildRenewalOpportunity(c);

Verify: Uplifted ARR = 107500.00, the renewal row is Status__c = 'Open', Renewal_Date__c = contract end date.

Phase 9 — Orders & Fulfillment

9.1 Create Orders from a Contracted Quote ★★

Goal: Create an Order from a contracted quote.

  1. One order from the quote: AccountId, Pricebook2Id, QuoteId, Total_ARR__c; copy quote lines to order products.
  2. Default Fulfillment_Status__c = 'Pending'.

Verify: Order + order products match the quote dollar-for-dollar and Total_ARR__c ties.

9.2 Track Fulfillment Status ★★

Goal: Drive Pending -> Shipped -> Delivered.

  1. Insert an order, then call OrderFulfillmentService.updateFulfillmentStatus(orders) (defaults to Pending).
  2. Call OrderFulfillmentService.advanceFulfillment(ids) twice — first to Shipped, then to Delivered (stamps Fulfillment_Date__c).

Verify: Final state Delivered with Fulfillment_Date__c = today; a third call is idempotent (terminal state).

Phase 10 — Billing, Invoicing & Revenue Recognition

10.1 Build a Billing Schedule ★★★

Goal: Split annual value into monthly revenue rows.

apex
Quote q = new Quote(Id = [SELECT Id FROM Quote LIMIT 1].Id,
    Total_ARR__c = 12500, Contract_Term_Months__c = 12,
    AccountId = [SELECT Id FROM Account LIMIT 1].Id);
List<Revenue_Schedule__c> rows = BillingScheduleService.buildBillingSchedule(q, 12);
Decimal total = 0;
for (Revenue_Schedule__c r : rows) { total += r.Amount__c; }
System.debug(rows.size() + ' rows, sum ' + total);

Verify: 12 rows, Recognition_Method__c = 'Straight Line', Status__c = 'Pending', sum of Amount__c equals 12500 exactly (remainder on month 12).

10.2 Recognize Revenue Over Time ★★★

Goal: Recognize matured rows and roll ARR to the account.

  1. Query Pending Revenue_Schedule__c rows (some dated in the past, some future).
  2. Call RevenueRecognitionService.recognizeRevenue(ids) on them, then RevenueRecognitionService.rollupAccountARR(accountIds) for the affected accounts.

Verify: Past-dated rows become Recognized with Recognized_Amount__c set; future rows stay Pending; Account.Current_ARR__c equals the recognized sum.

Phase 11 — Revenue Lifecycle Management (RLM)

11.1 Compare CPQ vs RLM Objects ★★

Goal: Build the object-mapping table.

  1. Two columns: Legacy CPQ (SBQQ__) vs Revenue Cloud / RLM (core).
  2. Map: SBQQ__Quote__c -> Quote, SBQQ__QuoteLine__c -> QuoteLineItem, SBQQ__ProductOption__c -> ProductCatalog + ProductCatalogItem, option constraints -> ProductSellingModel.

Verify: Every major quoting object has a row and you can state the migration direction (managed package to core on RLM) and why RLM is API-first.

11.2 Model a Subscription with RLM ★★★

Goal: Model a seat-based subscription on core objects.

  1. Define a product in ProductCatalog; attach a ProductSellingModel for per-seat quantity (1-500) and 12-month term; price 10 USD/seat/month in the price book.
  2. Write the SOQL enumerating cataloged products with their selling models (adjust field names to the API 68.0 schema in your org).

Verify: The catalog item exposes per-seat quantity, the price book quotes 10 USD / seat / month, and the SOQL runs clean.

Phase 12 — CPQ Automation & Integration

12.1 Publish and Subscribe to a Platform Event ★★★

Goal: Emit and consume Revenue_Sync__e.

apex
Revenue_Sync__e evt = new Revenue_Sync__e(
    Source_Object__c = 'Quote', Direction__c = 'Outbound', Status__c = 'Approved',
    Integration_Type__c = 'ApprovalSync', Endpoint__c = 'RevenueCloudEventBus',
    Payload__c = '{"quoteId":"QG2xx","approvalStatus":"Approved"}',
    Correlation_Id__c = String.valueOf(Crypto.getRandomLong()));
EventBus.publish(evt);

Verify: The subscriber fires exactly once (QuoteTriggerHandlerService.afterUpdate also publishes on approval change — check you are not double-publishing) and Direction__c = 'Outbound'.

12.2 Call an External Pricing API ★★★★

Goal: Fetch and apply an external price adjustment.

  1. Configure a Named Credential PricingService; reference it with callout:PricingService (never a hard-coded URL).
  2. POST quote totals and read back discountPercent, applying it only on a 200 response, guard against nulls.
apex
HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
req.setEndpoint('callout:PricingService/v1/quote/adjustment');
req.setMethod('POST'); req.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
req.setBody('{"totalARR": 250000, "region": "EMEA"}');
HttpResponse res = new Http().send(req);
if (res.getStatusCode() == 200) {
    Map<String, Object> body = (Map<String, Object>) JSON.deserializeUntyped(res.getBody());
    Decimal adj = Decimal.valueOf(String.valueOf(body.get('discountPercent')));
}

Verify: No DML until the callout returns, adjustment applied only on 200, named credential used, missing discountPercent handled.

Phase 13 — Reports, Dashboards & Revenue Analytics

13.1 Build an ARR Pipeline Report ★★

Goal: Report potential ARR by stage.

  1. Opportunity report grouped by StageName summing ARR__c with forecast category.
  2. Add quote-stage leakage (Quote.Total_ARR__c vs expected) and a funnel chart.

Verify: The report sums to open pipeline, ARR per stage is correct, and the funnel shows drop-off at quote approval -> closed won.

13.2 Design a Discount Leakage Dashboard ★★★

Goal: Surface how discounting erodes ARR.

soql
SELECT AVG(Discount_Percent__c) avgDisc, SUM(Total_ARR__c) arr
FROM Quote WHERE Approval_Status__c = 'Approved' GROUP BY Approval_Status__c
  1. Use this plus Opportunity.Discount_Leakage_Percent__c and Account.Current_ARR__c.
  2. Add a gauge for avg discount, a top-10 deepest discounts table, and a trend line.

Verify: Each tile reads a real field and the gauge equals your avgDisc.

Phase 14 — Certification Prep

14.1 Build a Domain-Weighted Study Plan ★

Goal: Turn blueprint weights into study hours.

  1. CPQ Specialist blueprint: CPQ Platform 23%, Bundle Configurations 17%, Pricing 16%, Orders/Contracts/Amendments/Renewals 15%, Products 11%, Quote Templates 7%, Product Selection 7%, Approvals 4%.
  2. Allocate hours proportionally (e.g. 40h -> 9.2h/6.8h/...) and tag which exercise ids cover each domain.

Verify: Weights sum to 100%, allocation matches, every domain has at least one exercise id.

14.2 Practice: Catalog & Bundle Questions ★★

Goal: Cement Products (11%) + Bundle Configurations (17%).

  1. Load 10 questions into Training_Question__c with Certification_Target__c = CPQ Specialist; answer, read Explanation__c, retake to 100%.

Verify: Correct answer letters set, in-app score reflects your answers.

14.3 Practice: Pricing & Discount Questions ★★

Goal: Cement Pricing (16%).

  1. Ten questions on price books, price rules, tier resolution (5.1/5.2 boundary behavior).

Verify: You can state the 25000/50000 tier boundaries from memory and score 100%.

14.4 Practice: Approvals & Renewals Questions ★★

Goal: Cement Approvals (4%) + Orders/Contracts/Amendments/Renewals (15%).

  1. Ten approval + renewal questions; re-run 7.x/8.x Apex to confirm the behavior you claimed.

Verify: You can state the 25% threshold rule and uplift formula ARR * (1 + uplift/100) and score 100%.

14.5 Practice: Billing & Revenue Questions ★★

Goal: Cement the billing/recognition side.

  1. Ten billing + recognition questions; re-run 10.1/10.2 for the remainder rule and straight-line behavior; review ASC 606 / IFRS 15 terms.

Verify: You can predict the month-12 remainder and Current_ARR__c roll-up, and score 100%.

Mini Projects

P1 Design an End-to-End CPQ Data Model ★★★

Goal: The ERD + data dictionary the rest of the portfolio uses.

  1. Inventory standard objects; add the custom objects and custom fields from the academy data model.
  2. Draw relationships with cardinality (flag the 1-1 quote->contract); list per-object rules (e.g. Amount_Non_Negative, quote approval status, valid correct answer).

Success criteria: A reviewer can navigate from any record back to its quote/opportunity without guessing, and every field used in these exercises is on the diagram.

P2 Configure a Configurable Product Bundle ★★★★

Goal: A working configurable bundle.

  1. Pick a real bundle; create option groups with "Group: Option" naming and single-select constraints.
  2. Enforce with validateBundleConfiguration / hasConflictingOptions; price as the sum of options via rollupBundlePrice.
  3. Add a Discount_Schedule__c volume tier and apply via PriceRuleEngineService.applyPriceRules.

Success criteria: Three valid configs price correctly, an invalid two-Storage config is rejected with a readable message, and a volume discount changes net prices.

P3 Implement a Discount Approval Matrix ★★★★

Goal: Route by amount and requester authority.

  1. Define authority as threshold records (rep to 10%, manager to 25%, executive above) mapped to Discount_Schedule__c-style data.
  2. Route with requiresApproval/determineApprover; persist each hop in Approval_Log__c; add the two-step chain from 7.2.
  3. Approve the quote only on the terminal hop.

Success criteria: 22% stops at manager, 30% triggers the full chain, every hop logged with Decision_Date__c, Approval_Status__c reflects the terminal decision.

P4 Build an Automated Quote Document ★★★

Goal: A branded PDF from a template.

  1. Template with header, line table, totals, terms, bound fields (account, quote number, Total_ARR__c).
  2. Add an approval status area bound to Approval_Status__c; generate for two accounts.

Success criteria: Both documents carry correct numbers, render Approved/Draft correctly, and regenerate after a price change.

P5 Automate Contract Generation & Renewal ★★★★

Goal: Trigger-driven contracts + renewals, safely.

  1. ContractGenerationService.generateContracts on won quotes; RenewalQuoteService.buildRenewalPipeline on near-expiry contracts.
  2. Wire through triggers with QuoteTriggerHandlerService.shouldRun/clear guards.

Success criteria: 5 won quotes -> 5 Draft contracts -> predicted renewals with uplift, no recursion loop.

P6 Create a Subscription Billing Schedule ★★★★

Goal: Order to monthly billing, idempotently.

  1. BillingScheduleService.createRevenueSchedules(orders); re-run to prove zero duplicates.
  2. Verify straight-line with remainder for non-divisible ARR; publish Revenue_Sync__e on creation.

Success criteria: term-months rows sum exactly to annual ARR, a second run creates nothing, correlation id unique per batch.

P7 Implement Revenue Recognition Automation ★★★★

Goal: Scheduled recognition + account roll-up.

  1. Scheduled Apex calling recognizeRevenue on matured rows and rollupAccountARR for their accounts.
  2. Add a dashboard row of Recognized vs Pending by period.

Success criteria: Past-dated rows flip on schedule, future rows untouched, Current_ARR__c ties to the recognized sum, dashboard shows the split.

P8 Build a Quote-to-Cash Integration ★★★★★

Goal: Quote events out to an ERP.

  1. Publish Revenue_Sync__e on approval change; subscribe and package the payload.
  2. Outbound callout to the ERP via Named Credential keyed by Correlation_Id__c.
  3. Record CPQ_Sync_Status__c / Order.ERP_Order_Number__c on success; use Retry_Count__c on failure.

Success criteria: exactly one event per approval, ERP success returns the order number, failures retry without duplicating the order.

P9 Design a Revenue Analytics Dashboard ★★★

Goal: One dashboard: ARR, leakage, recognition.

  1. ARR pipeline report (13.1), discount leakage drill-down, recognition by method/period.
  2. Compose with filters by Account.Region__c and Partner_Tier__c.

Success criteria: Every tile reads a real field, the tiles tie together, two filters change every chart.

P10 Migrate Legacy CPQ Data to RLM ★★★★★

Goal: Move SBQQ__ data to core objects.

  1. Inventory SBQQ__Quote__c, SBQQ__QuoteLine__c, SBQQ__ProductOption__c; map to Quote, QuoteLineItem, ProductCatalog/ProductSellingModel.
  2. Define transform rules (options -> selling-model features), stage, validate counts + sums, execute.

Success criteria: Post-migration counts match within tolerance, migrated quotes re-price identically via QuoteCalculatorService, validation report documents the delta.

Capstone

CAP Capstone: Enterprise Quote-to-Cash on Revenue Cloud ★★★★★

Goal: A full quote-to-cash flow on Revenue Cloud, presented end to end.

  1. Catalog 3 subscription products with selling models on core objects.
  2. Quote seats with bundle validation (BundleConfigurationService); price via PriceRuleEngineService; roll totals via QuoteCalculatorService.
  3. Route approval with matrix + chain (ApprovalRoutingService, Approval_Log__c).
  4. Contract + renewals (ContractGenerationService, RenewalQuoteService), order + fulfillment (OrderFulfillmentService), billing (BillingScheduleService).
  5. Recognize revenue (RevenueRecognitionService); publish Revenue_Sync__e on approval.
  6. Report pipeline ARR, leakage, recognition and renewal forecast; present with data model, key Apex, demo script.

Success criteria: One demo takes a quote from catalog to recognized revenue with correct numbers at every hop, all ten services are used, all custom objects/fields are in play, and the script explains the "why" at every stage — not just the click.

Return to the phase guide for the theory, and to the in-app answers panel for hints. Every id above — 1.1 through CAP — matches a "Show answer" entry exactly.
